$schema: Declarative runner-routing contract. Each lane binds a GitHub repo variable (`*_RUNS_ON_JSON`) to the label set it is INTENDED to route to, and to the kind of runner expected to serve it. Consumed by tools/scripts/runner_topology_check.py, which reconciles this file against the LIVE repo variables and LIVE registered runners, plus optional read-only TartCI profile/receipt/private-manifest fixtures. A lane whose labels no runner can satisfy is a routing black hole: jobs queue forever and GitHub reports no error. Editing a repo variable without editing its lane here is drift, and the checker fails on it. Docs: docs/guides/local-ci.md.
_note_expect: `expect` records the label set or declared off-switch sentinel the lane is CONTRACTED to use. It is the reviewed artifact: changing a repo variable is only legitimate when this file changes with it. `expect` is not automatically correct — a lane can be contracted to labels nothing serves, which is exactly the failure this checker exists to surface.
_note_github_hosted: Allowlist, not a heuristic. A `runs-on` value is treated as GitHub-hosted ONLY if every element appears here, so a typo ('macos-15x') fails loudly instead of being waved through as 'probably hosted'. GitHub's own discriminator is the literal `self-hosted` label: an array carrying it is a self-hosted label set. Both the scalar form (`runs-on: macos-15`) and the single-element array form (`runs-on: [macos-15]`) are legal hosted values and both are accepted here.
_note_sentinels: Magic values that mean 'this lane is deliberately switched off', not a label to route to. `build.yml` documents `local-only` as the explicit off switch for macOS overflow — emptiness cannot disable it, because GitHub treats unset and empty identically and the workflow's `||` default re-fills it.
_note_routing_controls: Exact-value controls that affect routing without being runs-on selectors. The overflow idle probe must target the same fast runner class as the required macOS selector; otherwise an idle rollback-only M1 can suppress overflow for work it cannot serve.
_note_event_class_v2: The repo variable remains the reviewed pre-dispatch selector. build.yml removes omit_labels and adds exactly one class label. TartCI source profiles declare assignment_mode, the post-transform base labels, and both tier rows, but no fixed priority: provider code derives 110 for merge-group and 100 for PR-head. Optional --fleet-profile/--fleet-receipt/--fleet-source-manifest fixtures let the checker reconcile source, installed receipt, and private desired-fleet evidence without querying a host or copying repo-specific labels into generic Shipyard/TartCI code.

service_evidence._why_queued_stall_seconds: Service history is a claim about the past and cannot expire, so a lane served for weeks and dead for hours still satisfies it — which is how a release lane with two releases stuck behind it reported 'the provisioner is alive and idle'. The queue is the only surface where a dead provisioner is visible while it is happening. The signal must be queue AGE, not queue presence: on a JIT lane the job queues FIRST and the provisioner then boots, so 'queued + no runner' is the ordinary transient and a check in that shape would fire on every burst. 1800s is derived from the fleet's own trigger — planning/fleet/local-macos-desired.json sets min_queued_age_seconds to 0 on m3/m5 and 600 on m1 — leaving a wide margin over the worst-case trigger plus VM boot and runner registration, so only a genuine stall crosses it.
service_evidence._why: Tart runners register JIT/ephemeral (tools/ci/tart-runner.sh, tart-runner-linux.sh): they exist only while a job runs and vanish when idle. So 'no runner carries this label' does NOT prove a black hole for an ephemeral lane — it may just be idle. Those lanes are judged on service history instead: has a job been dispatched to this exact label set recently? A label set with no runner AND no service has nothing provisioning it, which IS a black hole.
service_evidence._why_per_workflow: Evidence is gathered from the workflows that CONSUME the lane, not from a repo-wide run sweep. On a busy repo the newest 100 runs measured well under an hour of history, so a repo-wide scan would condemn any lane used less often than that — the release lanes fire per release, not per hour. Scoping to the consuming workflow makes 20 runs reach back months for a few API calls, and the scan is lazy: a lane with a live runner costs nothing.
service_evidence._why_lookback: 720h (30d) covers a normal release cadence with margin. A lane whose consuming workflow has not run at all in the window yields no evidence, which is reported as a black hole — see the honest-limits note in docs/guides/local-ci.md.

hosts._why: A lane check answers 'can these labels be served'. It cannot answer 'is this HOST still serving', and those came apart on m5: the host stayed registered and online while its disk filled, so every lane it backs kept reading healthy and m5 quietly served nothing for days. Nobody noticed until the queue did. The per-host census below is the missing half: it watches the one artifact that already proves a host served work, the runner_name and completed_at the jobs API reports for every job build.yml dispatched.
hosts._why_prefix_map: tartci fixes an ephemeral runner's name as <lane>-<supervisor pid>-<boot index>, so the lane prefix is the host identity and is stable across boots. This map is the one reviewed datum the census needs; everything else it computes from observation. Verified against 6h of live build.yml jobs on 2026-09-11: every self-hosted runner_name observed mapped to exactly one host, zero unmapped.
hosts._why_silence_hours: Long enough that an ordinary quiet stretch, a reboot, or a long single job cannot cross it; short enough that a host which stopped serving is found the same day rather than the same week.
hosts._why_demand_min_jobs: Silence alone is not a fault: an idle night is silence, and a fleet that pages on an idle night gets muted. The verdict needs DEMAND the host could have served and did not, measured as completed jobs on sibling hosts carrying a label set this host is observed to serve. Losing 5 consecutive placements across the whole window is implausible for a healthy host; raise this number rather than muting the rule if JIT races prove otherwise.
hosts._why_observation_hours: service_evidence.lookback_hours is 720h, which is right for a lane that fires per release and wrong here: build.yml alone holds over 16,000 runs and roughly 65 runs per 12h, so a 720h per-job walk would cost thousands of API calls every hour. 72h is bounded, covers a weekend, and is far past silence_hours. The walk is newest-first and exits as soon as every declared host has served inside silence_hours, so a healthy fleet pays a few dozen calls.
hosts._why_max_runs: A hard ceiling on the walk so an hourly cron cannot run away. Hitting it BEFORE the window is covered suppresses every silence verdict and reports degraded instead: a truncated window cannot distinguish a silent host from an unread one.
hosts._why_severity: Shadow mode. The census ships reporting to the step summary only (no issue, no assignee, no red run), so one week of hourly sweeps can count would-be fires against real traffic before anything pages. Promoting is a reviewed edit of this one value to "error" plus the per-host issue step in the workflow, and must not happen before the operator notification path is confirmed.
hosts._why_workflow: The fleet's whole macOS build and preamble load runs through build.yml, so it is where every host leaves evidence. Silence is judged on this repo's evidence only: a host also serving other repos' lanes is out of scope, and this rule deliberately does not claim the host is idle, only that it stopped serving pulp.

must_remain_unset.why: Namespace cloud macOS/Linux/Windows runners are a PAID overflow deliberately kept off for cost (CLAUDE.md 'Runner priority'). Setting one silently starts billing; pointing one at self-hosted labels dumps the high-volume sanitizer/coverage lanes onto the Mac Studios that host the required macOS gate. Break-glass only, operator-dispatched, never automatic.

lanes.purpose: The REQUIRED macOS gate. Every PR merge depends on this lane resolving. Routed to ephemeral tartci VMs (`pulp-build-vm`), NOT the persistent `pulp-build-studio` runners: a VM is clean per job, so the gate cannot inherit a warm build dir from an unrelated branch. That reuse is what produced the 2026-06-07 random-SEGFAULT cluster across many PRs at once, and `build.yml` sets `clean: false` on self-hosted, so the persistent runners keep their dirs by design.

Required-check alias job for `macos`. It is the LAST job in a build.yml run and does one terminal jobs-API read, so starving it does not merely delay a check: the run never reaches a terminal state, holds this ref's concurrency group, and leaves the next push's run at status `pending` with zero jobs. The `linux` and `windows` aliases already report from the self-hosted preamble for that reason; this lane gives `macos` the same protection without borrowing preamble capacity when a dedicated alias pool exists.
Cheap preamble/probe legs that gate the heavier build jobs.

macOS build overflow for saturated required work. CONTRACTED OFF: the operative value is the `local-only` sentinel, which pins overflow work to the local pool and is the documented off-switch in build.yml. Hosted `macos-15` overflow stays disabled for cost control (CLAUDE.md), so the sentinel is the intended steady state rather than a deviation from it. UNSETTING the variable is NOT the way to disable this lane: unset restores the `macos-15` hosted fallback recorded in unset_fallback, which is the opposite of the intent. Previously this lane contracted ["macos-15"] while the live value was the sentinel, so a severity:required lane sat at a permanent ERROR [drift] for an intended state -- a standing red that teaches readers to skim past the report and lets a genuine drift hide in the noise.

release-cli arm64 macOS build lane. SET to the dedicated `pulp-build-vm-release` ephemeral Tart pool — a proven dedicated release lane, served by JIT slots that register only while a job runs (judge it on service evidence, never the runner census; see service_evidence). Resolution in release-cli.yml is PULP_RELEASE_MACOS_RUNS_ON_JSON -> PULP_LOCAL_MACOS_RUNS_ON_JSON -> Namespace (off for cost) -> macos-15, so UNSETTING this variable is the break-glass rollback: releases then share the self-hosted Studio/M5 pool that backs the required `macos` gate — safe because release-cli is tag-only and its checkout runs clean:true, so it neither starves the gate nor inherits a warm dir (why the hosted-pool starvation incidents of 2026-05-18 and 2026-06-09 no longer block publishing). unset_fallback records that rollback labelset.

release-cli Intel/universal macOS leg, and the LOWEST-priority fallback in the darwin-x64 chain (PULP_RELEASE_DARWIN_X64_RUNS_ON_JSON -> PULP_RELEASE_MACOS_RUNS_ON_JSON -> this). Contracted to hosted macos-15 because darwin-x64 is CROSS-COMPILED on an Apple-Silicon runner rather than built on the native macos-15-intel image, which CPU-pegs and never shipped an artifact. The Mac mini native-Intel lane is PULP_NATIVE_INTEL_RUNS_ON_JSON and is a separate, advisory, still-unproven lane; it is not a substitute for this release leg.

Control-plane Linux job for release-cli.yml and sign-and-release.yml (resolve/publish coordination, not a binary build). Resolution is PULP_RELEASE_CONTROL_LINUX_RUNS_ON_JSON -> PULP_LOCAL_LINUX_RUNS_ON_JSON -> ubuntu-latest, so the Mac Pro Linux x64 lane is the next preference in the chain. Contracted hosted today: this job coordinates a release, and pointing it at the local lane is not a variable decision alone — the Mac Pro runners live in a RESTRICTED org runner group, so whether a given workflow may use them is governed by that group's workflow-ref restriction as well as by the selector. Set this only with a dispatch proof recorded for this specific consuming workflow.

Advisory native Intel build and test lane on the dedicated physical Mac mini. Its labels cannot match the required Apple-Silicon gate, and unsetting the variable immediately restores the hosted macos-15-intel fallback.

TSan lane, GitHub-hosted and clean per run, matching ASan and RTSan. The dedicated ephemeral VM lane (pulp-sanitizer-vm-macos) stays CONTRACTED OFF until its host passes a real dispatch proof: the supervisor host must carry the pulp-build-runner macOS golden, its GitHub queue scan must authenticate, and the tartci idle gate must be armed so the lane yields to the required macOS gate. Pointing this variable at the VM labels before that proof is a silent hang, not a failure: GitHub queues TSan forever and reports no error. See docs/guides/local-ci.md for the proof procedure.
ASan lane — GitHub-hosted, clean per run.
UBSan lane — GitHub-hosted on the current Apple Clang/libc++ toolchain, clean per run.
RTSan lane — GitHub-hosted, clean per run.
Coverage lane — GitHub-hosted, clean per run (warm-dir ODR keeps it off self-hosted).
Dispatch and release fallback Linux x86_64 lane served by repository-scoped ephemeral Proxmox VMs on macpro.
Automatic Linux x86_64 lane for protected build.yml and trusted dispatcher workflows through the restricted pulp-trusted-build runner group.

Required Vellum trusted-gate executor. It may use the restricted, ephemeral Mac Pro Linux lane when explicitly configured and falls back to ubuntu-latest when unset, preserving a routable protected-checkout path without making local capacity mandatory.
GCC compile gate (advisory). Native x86_64 Linux on the macpro Proxmox host; falls back to ubuntu-latest when unset.
IWYU advisory lane. Native x86_64 Linux on macpro; falls back to ubuntu-24.04 when unset.
Public-headers-compile-standalone advisory lane. Native x86_64 Linux on macpro; falls back to ubuntu-24.04 when unset.
Linux primary target. Not referenced by any workflow today; kept for the reroute/overflow tooling.
Linux overflow to the M5 host. Not referenced by any workflow today.
Windows build lane via QEMU on the Mac Studio host. Not referenced by any workflow today.
Windows primary target. Not referenced by any workflow today.
Windows overflow to the M5 host. Not referenced by any workflow today.
